s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with vomiting and abnormal cardiac findings
salient_findings: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Reversed position of the heart chambers
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 80s
Chest pain duration is 1 hour
Patient denies history of hypertension and diabetes
Temperature is 36°C
Heart rate is 79 beats per minute
Blood pressure is 92/56 mm Hg
Maximal cardiac impulse is in the right fifth interspace
Hepatic dullness is located in the left subcostal region
Initial serum troponin I level is 0.070 ng/mL
ECG shows negative P waves in lead I
ECG shows QRS complexes with activation of ventricle in right thorax
ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Coronary Angiography shows total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Transthoracic Echocardiogram shows reversed position of the heart chambers

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery and elevated serum troponin I level

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
shortlist.why_kept: Reversed position of the heart chambers and maximal cardiac impulse in the right fifth interspace

shortlist.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: ECG shows ST-segment elevations and elevated serum troponin I level

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG shows negative P waves in lead I and QRS complexes with activation of ventricle in right thorax

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, vomiting, elevated serum troponin I level, and ST-segment elevations in multiple ECG leads, along with the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery seen on coronary angiography, are all consistent with an acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: While the patient has a reversed position of the heart chambers, this is not a disease entity that explains the acute presentation of chest pain and elevated troponin.

rejected.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
rejected.why: This is a possible cause of the acute myocardial infarction but does not fully explain the clinical presentation and laboratory findings as a standalone diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's ECG and laboratory findings, including the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, are more suggestive of an acute myocardial infarction than myocarditis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette to support this diagnosis, such as characteristic ECG changes or imaging findings of right ventricular dysfunction.
